newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile oil company Enap signs $150 mln loan.
newsitem.headline: Chile oil company Enap signs $150 mln loan.

text.p: Chilean state company Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (Enap) signed Wednesday a $150 million syndicated loan with a group of 10 foreign banks led by Spanish bank Argentaria.
The credit was a bullet loan payable in the fifth year with an interest rate of 0.225 percent above LIBOR, said officials.
The company, Chile's only oil producer, will use the funds to refinance short term debt and to finance new investments, said general manager Alvaro Garcia at the signing ceremony.
Other banks involved in the loan included Dresdner Bank, Bank of America and the Royal Bank of Canada.
Enap and its international division Sipetrol will invest around $230 million next year, part of which will be financed by new international loans, said Garcia.
"The level of investment will be similar to this year ($180 million) and another $50 million or $60 million for Sipetrol," he said.

Enap operates oil wells in the far southern Straits of Magellan. Sipetrol carries out exploration in Ecuador, Venezuela and Colombia and is prospecting for oil in the Atlantic in a joint venture with Argentine energy firm YPF SA.
